translations.literal: The Han general, the Marquis of Gonggao Yi Dang, sent the king a letter, saying: "By decree we execute the unrighteous; those who surrender shall be pardoned of their crimes and restored to their former state;
translations.idiomatic: The Han general, the Marquis of Gonggao Yi Dang, sent the king a letter, saying, "By decree we execute the unrighteous; those who surrender shall be pardoned of their crimes and restored to their former state;

sentences.zh: 不降者滅之。

translations.literal: Not surrender exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who do not surrender shall be annihilated.

sentences.zh: 王何處，須以從事。」

translations.literal: Where will the king go? We await your decision."
translations.idiomatic: Where will the king go? We await your orders."

sentences.zh: 王肉袒叩頭漢軍壁，謁曰：「臣卬奉法不謹，驚駭百姓，乃苦將軍遠道至于窮國，敢請菹醢之罪。」

translations.literal: The king, baring his flesh, kowtowed at the Han army's rampart and presented himself, saying: "Your subject Ang was not careful in upholding the law, startled and terrified the people, and has toiled the general to come on a long road to this poor kingdom—I dare request the crime of being pickled and minced."
translations.idiomatic: The king, baring his flesh, kowtowed at the Han army's rampart and presented himself, saying, "Your subject Ang was not careful in upholding the law, startled and terrified the people, and has toiled the general to come on a long road to this poor kingdom—I dare request the crime of being pickled and minced."

sentences.zh: 弓高侯執金鼓見之，曰：「王苦軍事，願聞王發兵狀。」

translations.literal: The Marquis of Gonggao, holding drum and bell, received him and said: "The king has toiled in military affairs; I wish to hear the circumstances of Your Majesty's raising troops."
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Gonggao, holding drum and bell, received him and said, "The king has toiled in military affairs; I wish to hear the circumstances of Your Majesty's raising troops."

sentences.zh: 王頓首膝行對曰：「今者，晁錯天子用事臣，變更高皇帝法令，侵奪諸侯地。

translations.literal: The king kowtowed, advancing on his knees, and replied: "Now Chao Cuo is the Son of Heaven's minister in power; he has changed and raised Emperor Gao's laws and commands and invaded and seized the feudal lords' lands.
translations.idiomatic: The king kowtowed, advancing on his knees, and replied, "Now Chao Cuo is the Son of Heaven's minister in power; he has changed and raised Emperor Gao's laws and commands and invaded and seized the feudal lords' lands.

sentences.zh: 卬等以為不義，恐其敗亂天下，七國發兵，且以誅錯。

translations.literal: Ang etc. considered unrighteous, feared his defeat disorder realm, seven kingdoms sent troops, moreover to execute Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and the others considered these acts unjust and feared they would bring ruin to the realm. The seven kingdoms raised their armies with the stated purpose of punishing Chao Cuo.

sentences.zh: 今聞錯已誅，卬等謹以罷兵歸。」

translations.literal: Now that we have heard Chao Cuo has already been executed, Ang and the others respectfully stop our troops and return."
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have heard Chao Cuo has already been executed, we, Ang and the others, respectfully halt our troops and return."

sentences.zh: 將軍曰：「王茍以錯不善，何不以聞？

translations.literal: The general said: "If the king considered Chao Cuo not good, why did you not report it?
translations.idiomatic: The general said, "If the king considered Chao Cuo not good, why did you not report it?

sentences.zh: （及）［乃］未有詔虎符，擅發兵擊義國。

translations.literal: There was no imperial decree or tiger tally, yet you arbitrarily sent troops and attacked righteous states.
translations.idiomatic: Without an imperial decree or tiger tally, you sent out troops on your own authority and attacked loyal states.

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，意非欲誅錯也。」

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, your intention was not to execute Chao Cuo."
translations.idiomatic: Seen from this, your real intention was not to execute Chao Cuo."

sentences.zh: 乃出詔書為王讀之。

translations.literal: Then took out decree document for king read it.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced the imperial edict and read it aloud to the king.

sentences.zh: 讀之訖，曰：「王其自圖。」

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, he said: "Your Majesty must decide for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, he said, "Your Majesty must decide for yourself."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「如卬等死有餘罪。」

translations.literal: The king said: "Ang and the others deserve to die many times over."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "Ang and the others deserve to die many times over."

sentences.zh: 遂自殺。

translations.literal: Then suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 太后、太子皆死。

translations.literal: Empress dowager, crown prince all died.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and the crown prince both perished as well.

sentences.zh: 膠東、菑川、濟南王皆死，國除，納于漢。

translations.literal: Jiaodong, Zichuan, Jinan kings all died, kingdoms removed, incorporated into Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Kings of Jiaodong, Zichuan, and Jinan all died. Their kingdoms were abolished, and their territories were absorbed into the Han domain.

sentences.zh: 酈將軍圍趙十月而下之，趙王自殺。

translations.literal: Li general surrounded Zhao ten months then took it, Zhao king suicide.
translations.idiomatic: General Li besieged Zhao for ten months before taking it. The King of Zhao killed himself.

sentences.zh: 濟北王以劫故，得不誅，徙王菑川。

translations.literal: Jibei king because coercion reason, got not executed, moved king Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jibei, because he had been coerced, was spared execution and was transferred to rule as the King of Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 初，吳王首反，并將楚兵，連齊趙。

translations.literal: Initially, Wu king first rebelled, united led Chu troops, connected Qi Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, the King of Wu was the first to rebel. He took command of the forces of Chu and forged alliances with Qi and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 正月起兵，三月皆破，獨趙後下。

translations.literal: First month raised troops, three months all broken, only Zhao later surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The revolt began in the first month and within three months all the rebels had been crushed. Only Zhao held out and fell later.

sentences.zh: 復置元王少子平陸侯禮為楚王，續元王後。

translations.literal: Again established Yuan wang youngest son Pinglu marquis Li as Chu king, continued Yuan wang descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Li, the Marquis of Pinglu and youngest son of the former King Yuan, was appointed as the new King of Chu to carry on King Yuan's line.

sentences.zh: 徙汝南王非王吳故地，為江都王。

translations.literal: Moved Runan king Fei king Wu old lands, became Jiangdu king.
translations.idiomatic: Fei, the King of Runan, was transferred to rule over the former territories of Wu and became the King of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：吳王之王，由父省也。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: The King of Wu's enfeoffment as king arose from his father's reduction in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: The King of Wu owed his kingship to his father's demotion.

sentences.zh: 能薄賦斂，使其眾，以擅山海利。

translations.literal: Able reduce taxes levies, command his multitude, monopolize mountain sea profits.
translations.idiomatic: He was able to keep taxes light, command the loyalty of his people, and monopolize the profits of the mountains and the sea.

sentences.zh: 逆亂之萌，自其子興。

translations.literal: Contrary disorder sprouts, from his son arose.
translations.idiomatic: The seeds of his rebellion first stirred with the death of his son.

sentences.zh: 爭技發難，卒亡其本；

translations.literal: He quarreled over a game and provoked disaster, and finally lost his foundation;
translations.idiomatic: A quarrel over a game brought calamity on him, and in the end he lost the foundation of his house;

sentences.zh: 親越謀宗，竟以夷隕。

translations.literal: He drew close to the Yue and plotted against the imperial clan; in the end he perished at the hands of the Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted himself to the Yue and plotted against the imperial house, only to perish at the hands of those very barbarians.

sentences.zh: 晁錯為國遠慮，禍反近身。

translations.literal: Cuo for state far consideration, calamity instead near body.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo planned far ahead for the sake of the state, yet calamity fell upon his own person.

sentences.zh: 袁盎權說，初寵後辱。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang authority persuasion, initially favored later humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang relied on persuasion and expedience, winning favor at first but meeting disgrace in the end.

sentences.zh: 故古者諸侯地不過百里，山海不以封。

translations.literal: Therefore, ancient feudal lords lands not exceed hundred li, mountain sea not with enfeoff.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, therefore, a feudal lord's territory did not exceed a hundred li, and mountains and seas were never granted as fiefs.

sentences.zh: 「毋親夷狄，以疏其屬」，蓋謂吳邪？

translations.literal: "Do not be close to the Yi and Di lest you estrange your own kin"—was this not speaking of Wu?
translations.idiomatic: "Do not draw close to the Yi and Di and thereby estrange your own kin"—surely this speaks of Wu?

sentences.zh: 「毋為權首，反受其咎」，豈盎、錯邪？

translations.literal: "Do not be the head of intrigue lest you receive its blame in return"—was this not Yuan Ang and Chao Cuo?
translations.idiomatic: "Do not stand at the head of intrigue, lest its blame return upon you"—surely this speaks of Yuan Ang and Chao Cuo?
